content_units: 20-Minute Home Exercise Plan for Mild Knee Osteoarthritis

This routine is designed for a   beginner  ,   low-impact  ,   at-home   schedule:   20 minutes per session, 4 days per week  . It prioritizes joint mobility, gentle leg strength, and steady cardiovascular work while being mindful of   morning stiffness   and   blood pressure medication use  .
4-Day Beginner Routine
Day   Focus   20-Minute Plan   Key Benefit
Day 1   Mobility + Light Strength   4 min easy warm-up; 6 min knee-friendly mobility; 8 min band/leg strengthening; 2 min cool-down   Reduces stiffness; builds support around the knee
Day 2   Stationary Bike   3 min easy start; 12 min comfortable pedaling; 3 min slightly easier pace; 2 min cool-down   Improves circulation and joint-friendly cardio
Day 3   Mobility + Light Strength   4 min warm-up; 6 min flexibility/motion work; 8 min strength; 2 min cool-down   Better function for stairs, standing, walking
Day 4   Bike + Balance   3 min easy start; 10 min bike; 5 min balance and sit-to-stand work; 2 min cool-down   Builds endurance and confidence
Session Details
Warm-up ideas, 3-4 minutes
- March in place slowly while holding a chair if needed
- Gentle heel raises
- Seated knee extensions without weight
- Easy shoulder rolls and ankle circles
Mobility work, about 6 minutes
- Seated knee straighten/bend:   8-10 reps each leg
- Heel slides on floor or bed:   8-10 reps each leg
- Calf stretch at wall:   20-30 seconds each side
- Hamstring stretch seated:   20-30 seconds each side
- Gentle quad set: tighten thigh with leg straight, hold   3-5 seconds  ,   8 reps
Strength work, about 8 minutes
- Sit-to-stand from a chair:   6-10 reps
- Standing hip abduction with band or no band:   8-10 reps each side
- Standing hamstring curl:   8-10 reps each side
- Mini-squats holding chair, very shallow:   6-8 reps
- Side steps with light band:   6-10 steps each direction
Bike work
- Start at   very easy resistance
- Aim for a pace where he can still speak in full sentences
- If knees feel good after 1-2 weeks, add   1-2 minutes   or a small increase in resistance
Cool-down, 2 minutes
- Slow walking or very easy pedaling
- Gentle calf and hamstring stretch
- 3-4 slow breaths
Safety Notes for Knee OA and Blood Pressure
-   Best time to exercise:   often   later in the morning   or after a warm shower if he wakes up stiff.
-   Pain rule:   mild discomfort is common, but pain should stay around   0-3/10   and settle within   24 hours  .
-   Avoid deep knee bending   early on, especially painful squats, kneeling, twisting, or sudden pivots.
-   Use support:   chair, countertop, or wall for balance during standing exercises.
-   Go slow with position changes:   lisinopril can sometimes make people feel lightheaded when standing up quickly.
-   Breathe continuously:   do not hold his breath during band or chair exercises.
-   Footwear:   supportive shoes help reduce knee stress.
-   Progress gradually:   increase only   one thing at a time  —reps, resistance, or time.
-   Rest day spacing:   a good pattern is   Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat   or similar.
Practical starting level
- Week 1-2: do   1 set   of each strength move
- Week 3-4: increase to   2 sets   if pain and swelling stay controlled
- Keep bike resistance low until he tolerates sessions well
When He Should Stop and Contact a Clinician
Stop the session and seek clinician guidance if he has:
-   Chest pain
-   Shortness of breath that feels unusual or severe
-   Dizziness, faintness, or feeling like he may pass out
-   New irregular heartbeat or strong palpitations
-   Sudden major knee swelling
-   Knee pain that is sharp, worsening, or causes limping
-   Pain lasting more than 24 hours after exercise
-   A locked knee  , giving way, or inability to bear weight
-   Calf swelling, warmth, or pain
-   A big blood pressure spike or unusually severe headache   if he monitors BP and notices major changes
Brief context note

This is general educational guidance, not a diagnosis or personal medical clearance plan. With knee osteoarthritis and blood pressure treatment, a clinician or physical therapist can tailor it further if symptoms flare.
